sources.title: European yew: selected female shoot study
sources.scope: Selected actual Kew species profile through search retrieval: densely branching evergreen, dark pointed linear leaves appearing two-ranked, individual dark seed in open-tipped fleshy red aril. An aril is not an ordinary pine cone or angiosperm fruit.

retrieval.accessMethod: Selected institutional botanical description through web retrieval; direct local HTML unavailable

findings.shape: A detailed selected female leafy shoot has flattened pointed dark-green leaves appearing in two ranks, branching woody axes, an open-tipped red fleshy aril and a separate dark exposed seed. It represents an organ study rather than a complete old yew tree.
findings.surface: Original numerical connected woody/green axes, individual curved leaf surfaces, subdued pigment variation and selected reproductive surfaces. No source photograph pixels or measured tissue optical parameters.
findings.movement: Same retained woody axes, rachises, leaves and reproductive surfaces during small authored external deflection. Root/support position and scale remain anchored. Timing and angles are qualitative; there is no wind/elasticity solver, physiological simulation or measured biomechanics. Complete germination, organ emergence and seed-to-adult development are unavailable; no resizing of a ready mature plant.
findings.evidenceScope: Selected actual Kew species profile through search retrieval: densely branching evergreen, dark pointed linear leaves appearing two-ranked, individual dark seed in open-tipped fleshy red aril. An aril is not an ordinary pine cone or angiosperm fruit.
corrections: Replaced the generic whole conifer with a detailed selected female leafy shoot and open red arils surrounding visible darker seeds.
Reduced oversized arils, narrowed pointed linear leaves, varied leaf length/roll/insertion and offset the apparent two-ranked display from spiral attachment.
Added attached short aril-bearing shoots and elevated diagnostic viewing so the open aperture and leaf surfaces can be seen.
findings.residual: This is a selected female shoot, not a complete mature tree or male reproductive form. Leaves, twig branching and arils remain numerically smooth/regular; stomata, tissue optics, exact dimensions, seed development and old bark are not reconstructed or measured. Partial occlusion is visible in some views.

assessmentRubric.identity: Accepted species-rank taxonomic concept and source-labelled authentic photograph; not independently redetermined

assessmentRubric.surface: Original numerical pigment and geometry, not calibrated photographic tissue optics
assessmentRubric.movement: Retained branch/rachis articulation; full development and environmental mechanics unavailable

limits: Partly stylized original educational reconstructions. Fine morphology, age variation, tissue optics, dimensions and environmental mechanics remain incomplete or unmeasured.
